What are the election fraud allegations roiling Israel? Could they change the results? — Noam Lehmann, Times of Israel, October 29, 2026 (explainer)
"Israeli political parties are strictly prohibited from receiving donations from noncitizens"; violations face fines and potential criminal prosecution.
Allegations involve suspected "Qatari funds allegedly used to encourage Arab voters to go to the polls"; Qatar denies.
"Election results have never been overturned in Israel, and if these allegations go to court, it would not delay the swearing-in of the new Knesset."
A court can annul votes at specific polling stations but has "never annulled an entire election."
"Offering people cash or favors to vote or refrain from voting is illegal," though the law permits driving voters to polls.
Petitions must be filed within 14 days of final results and can only proceed if allegations could "materially change the result of the election."
